objective: Fix confirmed M1 reference handover discontinuity and simulation clock jitter; validate measured acceleration/jerk using real Gazebo while preserving motion safety and semantic evidence boundaries.
acceptance: In simulation, embedded ControllerManager uses supplied simulation time consistently; hardware steady-clock behavior remains unchanged. Source revision and patch are pinned and reproducibly built as an isolated project-container overlay.

Stop/hold preserves the accepted trajectory prefix and absolute epoch through a future C2 splice. Feedback, deadline, scene and limit gates remain fail-closed. Invalid or stale replacements never become successful physical evidence.

Real seeded Gazebo tests compare baseline, clock-only fix and final combined fix; position/velocity/acceleration/jerk are reported with original thresholds. No smoothing or relaxed limits may hide spikes.
Existing contracts, scenarios, event persistence and replay remain passing; only M1 is implemented.
evidence: Before/after real Gazebo JSONL, summary metrics and GUI logs
Upstream source revision, local patch SHA256 and runtime library identity
Regression tests plus required project gates
stop_conditions: A change requires a public schema or hardware command
A required safety bound or measurement is unavailable
A runtime result would need to be replaced by fabricated physics evidence
